background_notes.fact: For a measure mu and finitely many integrable real functions f_i with real constants a_i, sum_i a_i f_i is integrable and its integral equals sum_i a_i integral f_i. Pointwise equal real integrands have equal integrals, and the zero function has integral zero. Apply with mu=dx, f_0(x)=dot(V(x,t0),A(x,t0)), f_j(x)=dot(Psp(j,x,t0),W(j,x,t0)) and g_j(x)=dot(V(x,t0),Ssp(j,x,t0)).

background_notes.justification: The Lebesgue integral is additive and real homogeneous on integrable real functions: positive/negative-part decomposition gives these identities with finite quantities, and induction gives the finite-sum form. Absolute integrability of combinations follows from the triangle inequality. Equality of functions preserves their integral; the integral of zero is zero even on an infinite-measure space. These facts justify exactly the displayed finite rearrangements, without an infinite sum or limiting interchange.

background_notes.justification: HasDerivAt asserts existence of the real derivative with the stated value, giving differentiability.
